Scope: roads and paving, potable water, TSE, sewer, storm water, irrigation and landscaping, electrical (medium voltage, telecom, street lighting) and CCTV networks in Zones A and G, over 18 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. On 23-Nov-2026 the project is 55.6% complete against 50.6% planned, 5.0% ahead (SPI 1.10). This week it gained 5.38% against 1.93% planned (2.8 times the plan), so the lead widened from 1.6% to 5.0%, ending five weekly drops in a row. Storm water (28,610 man-hours) and sewer works (12,010) earned two thirds of the week's man-hours, while procurement lost 2,990 man-hours. The storm water, sewer, TSE and potable water networks are ahead; road works are 0.7% behind, and procurement, engineering, electrical works and CCTV are further behind. The schedule update now forecasts completion 160 days after the contract date, 7 days later than last week.

Well ahead on progress, but the forecast finish slipped another week, to 160 days late. The P6 update of 23-Nov-2026 and the weekly report both forecast completion on 12-Dec-2027, 160 days after the contract date of 05-Jul-2027 (05-Dec-2027 last week). Every open P6 milestone moved by exactly 7 days, the same as the data date, so the week's high output did not shorten the critical path. The most negative float (−161 days) is still on the unit substations: their delivery now runs to 03-Mar-2027 and the transformer approvals have not started. Procurement fell to 58.4% against 100% planned (SPI 0.58): MV cables (0 of 51,500 m), unit substations, street lighting poles and lighting panels are not delivered, and the final substation location is still pending between the Client and SEC.

Data notes

  • The uploaded files name the project "Phase Two – Part Two" (SUD1-02-011), while the repository folder and the project tracker call it Phase 3 (المرحلة الثالثة).
  • The summary sheet labels cost-based progress as "Plan" and "Actual". This report uses physical progress (man-hour weighted) only: 50.58% planned and 55.59% actual.
  • The Physical-Chart Data sheet's baseline plans 52.5% at 06-Nov and 60.4% at 06-Dec, while the front sheet plans 50.58% to 23-Nov, below even the 06-Nov value. The chart shows the 23-Nov actual (55.59%) on the 06-Nov point.
  • Storm water earned 28,610 man-hours this week (15.3% of its budget; Zone A from 34.0% to 55.8%) and sewer 12,010 (19.3%; Zone A from 60.4% to 90.3%), but the Major Quantities sheet adds only 45 catch basins and 10 manholes and no GRP, UPVC or HDPE pipe. The jump should be checked against measured quantities.
  • Procurement earned −2,990 man-hours this week (60.44% to 58.42%), with no explanation and no change in the Procurement or Major Quantities delivery figures except 10 more manholes delivered.
  • The front sheet leaves physical progress for electrical, landscape and CCTV works blank; the man-hours in the Progress sheet were used. The front sheet's BOQ values for CCTV Zone A and Zone G read 46,056 and 2 SAR instead of 6,513,996 and 2,791,854. TSE now has 844 planned man-hours to date (0.96%), which gives an SPI of 15.7; it is shown as – in the phase table.
  • The P6 update counts 936 completed, 403 in progress and 776 not started (2,115). The Schedule sheet gives 963 completed with the same 403 and 776, which adds up to 2,142, and the front sheet still shows 144 in progress.
  • In the P6 update the project finishes on 12-Dec-2027, 160 days after the contract date, but its float is −138 days, and 82 open activities (mostly pipe bedding, pipe laying and testing) are scheduled to finish after 12-Dec-2027, the last on 18-Apr-2028 (96 last week).
  • The summary page's scope table shows 0 executed for every network, and its totals differ from the hidden Conclusion sheet (for example roads 15,234 m vs 18,252 m). Manholes are labelled "m" in the Major Quantities sheet but are counted in units.
  • Procurement figures disagree: street lighting poles are 590 units and 10% complete in the Procurement sheet but 592 units with 1 delivered in Major Quantities; LV cables are 29,700 m vs 68,400 m. MV cables are "not submitted" in procurement, while the risk register says they have been procured.
  • November manual head count fell from 458 to 295 between the two reports for the same month, while the trade table gives 358 for the manual trades, the same as the total head count including non-manual staff.
  • Field inspection requests closed fell from 4,430 to 4,144 while issued rose from 4,558 to 4,692, so open FIRs rose from 128 to 548. Processed shop drawings fell from 364 to 342: 22 road-work drawings moved from "approved as noted" to pending.
  • Several cells show #REF! errors (EAC, risk scores, safety score in the status score). The substation risk carries a value of 6,835,460.61 SAR, which is the landscape BOQ value.
  • The issue log repeats entries: IDs 3124 and 3125 are each used twice (observations 23 and 25, 24 and 26), and the rain-water and road-diversion observations of 14 and 15-Nov are each logged twice; the risk register repeats them in the same way. The front sheet's top-issues table pairs each observation with another observation's action (for example asphalt waste with "providing support to the loose soil").
  • Several sheets (front sheet header, Major Quantities, Physical-Chart Data) still carry 19-Oct-2026 as their date and the Milestones sheet 09-Oct-2026, although the report's data date is 23-Nov-2026; the Procurement sheet has not changed since 26-Oct. The report week is the contract week the report states (46 of 78); whole weeks since handover give 45.
